ai.summary: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017, which the company says improves benchmark performance and task speed while producing shorter outputs. The update is available on its website, app and developer platform.
ai.title: DeepSeek Pushes Out Updated AI Model It Says Is Faster, Leaner

ai.summary: China proposed export controls covering 23 AI technologies, including models, agents and computing clusters, citing national security concerns. The draft allows public consultation through November 15; the proposal excludes technology already public through open-source releases or academic papers.
ai.title: Beijing seeks tighter grip on AI exports amid US rivalry

ai.summary: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark said AI capabilities are advancing quickly and called for international cooperation on serious rules. He cited an internal model projecting that AI could raise U.S. economic output to $44 trillion by 2030, while noting that figure sounds “very outlandish.”
ai.title: Anthropic's Clark says AI's impact accelerating quickly and could vastly boost US GDP

quantum.source: Google Quantum AI / Science (reported by Phys.org)
quantum.summary: Google researchers demonstrated magic-state cultivation on its Willow processor, reducing errors in prepared magic states roughly 40-fold and reporting 99.99% logical fidelity. The result addresses a major error-correction bottleneck, though it is not a demonstration of a large-scale fault-tolerant computer.
quantum.title: Quantum magic state cleanup cuts errors 40-fold in first successful hardware test

quantum.summary: Anthropic reported that Claude designed quantum circuits for eight tasks across areas including chemistry, optimization, simulation and number theory, improving on prior published designs. One elliptic-curve circuit used about 17 times fewer gates, with a 12% increase in qubits; the designs have not been demonstrated on quantum hardware.
quantum.title: Anthropic's Claude Designs Quantum Circuits Requiring Up To 17x Fewer Gates

quantum.summary: A report describes IBM Research using collaborating AI agents to speed up high-level-synthesis estimates for quantum error-correction hardware design by 52 times, at a reported inference cost of $26. The work aims to make it faster and cheaper to explore chip architectures.
quantum.title: Quantum Zeitgeist Weekly Digest October 17th
